coordinates.object_orientation: Coiling plane XZ, coil axis Y; long fossil dimension Z, shorter X, thickness Y. Lowest pointZ0. Orient mineral-filled terminal end toward lower-left (-X,-Z) in front view, like Geiseltal image; nodes visible on upper margin.

view_roles.front: lateral shell face, comparable to real photographs
view_roles.side: edge/ventral thickness and terminal profile, inferred shape constrained by measured width
view_roles.top: ventral band and paired shoulder nodosity
view_roles.perspective: combined whorl, umbilicus, shoulders and solid terminal end

concept.reason: Four real photos from three identified C. nodosus specimens plus numerical dimensions constrain genus-level form. They are not four orthogonal angles of one individual. No extra concept image needed or generated.

original_scope: Compact broad whorls with strong shoulder nodes and subdued lateral ribbing. Original genus-level fossil-form interpretation informed by identified C. nodosus specimens, NOT an exact single-specimen replica.

reference_anchor.shape: Ceratites nodosus photographed by Haplochromis, Geiseltalmuseum, Commons original. Strong marginal nodes visible along upper outer silhouette; weak broad lateral relief on final body chamber.
reference_anchor.scale: MHNT.PAL.CEP.2001.105, Didier Descouens / Muséum de Toulouse; published dimensions 14 x 11.5 x 4 cm. Separate specimen, used explicitly as plausible genus-size/thickness anchor, not falsely attributed dimensions of the Geiseltal fossil.
reference_anchor.corroboration: Smithsonian USNM EO55285, two lateral views with CM ruler; same genus/species, middle Triassic, Ostwestfalen-Lippe Germany.
reference_anchor.age: Middle Triassic; Upper Muschelkalk context for MHNT specimen
reference_anchor.limitations: No true ventral orthographic photo of selected Geiseltal specimen. Cross-section uses MHNT thickness and smooth conservative interpolation; bilateral organization is anatomical inference.

scale.evidence: MHNT catalogued overall dimensions 140 x 115 x 40 mm. Long diameter maps Z, shorter in-plane span X, axial thickness Y. These are design dimensions based on a different identified individual, NOT measurements of Geiseltal photograph.
scale.tolerance: About +/-10% simplified outline; thickness should remain near 0.29 of long diameter, not spherical or paper-flat. No inferred genus maximum.

morphology: Planispiral compact ammonoid disk; progressively enlarged outer whorl encloses most early coil but leaves a small recessed umbilical region. No gastropod tower, separated spring, or donut torus.
Outer whorl broad in lateral projection with flattened-to-rounded flanks and rounded ventral band. Maintain real three-dimensional thickness about 4cm at14cm long diameter.

Strong short pointed/blunt shoulder nodes break the upper and early outer-whorl silhouette, blending continuously into whorl surface. Not long free spines, not random decorative beads. Keep lateral rib relief much weaker than these nodes.

Nodosity is not an invariant picket fence around the whole adult terminal chamber: Geiseltal reference shows conspicuous upper nodes but smoother expanded terminal portion. Use a restrained graduated node series and weaken it on final chamber. Exact count is simplification, not claimed measurement.
Sutures visible in fossils are septal contact lines, NOT structural ribs or decorative raised zigzag cords. Omit intricate sutures at this low-poly scale rather than turn them into ribs.

Terminal preserved whorl is a mineral-filled broken/truncated end. Preserve low uneven termination and very shallow end boundary if needed, never invent a deep empty aperture, intact lip, tentacles, eye or living tissue.

Small central loss in photos is taphonomic damage; do not drill a large through-hole. Use recessed umbilicus with a conservative small closed early coil. No museum labels, pins, ruler, photo texture, cracks copied point-for-point or pedestal.
uncertainty: Actual unseen ventral curvature and back face remain inferred from bilateral ammonoid anatomy plus measured thickness, not four observed photographic angles.
Node count, exact cross-section, and minor damage are simplified. Geiseltal shape and MHNT scale are different specimens; final references and description must disclose genus-level interpretation.
Fossil mineral colour is artistic matte tan/grey. No claims of living colour, original shell surface or pristine mouth anatomy.
palette: Matte restrained grey/tan stone, no photographic textures.
acceptance_focus: Front (-Y): compact broad outer whorl, modest umbilical recess, strong upper shoulder nodes against weaker lateral relief; distinguish from generic ribbed ammonite.
Side (+X): substantial but non-globular axial thickness, integrated shoulder nodes on both flanks; no disconnected spikes.
Top (+Z): rounded ventral band, bilateral organization and non-paper-flat shell thickness; avoid a sharp keel.
Perspective: whorl continuous, nodes locally integrated, final chamber smoother and terminal mineral-filled end not fabricated hollow mouth.
Four actual rendered views; two isolated deterministic rebuilds; pinned local dependencies. Prep readiness is not scientific/model QA PASS.
